description: Always-running queue → transform → sink asset. Compute is a bounded (or unbounded) consumer loop, not a sensor firing per-batch. Emits one AssetMaterialization heartbeat per batch. Pair with StreamingRunHealthSensorComponent for auto-restart. v1 supports queue.kind: kafka.

queue.label: Queue
queue.description: Queue config. v1: `{kind: kafka, topic, bootstrap_servers OR bootstrap_servers_env_var, group_id, auto_offset_reset?, value_deserializer?: json|utf-8|bytes, extra_config?, sasl_*/ssl_*?}`.

batch_timeout_ms.label: Batch Timeout (ms)
batch_timeout_ms.description: Max wait per batch before flushing partial (ms).

max_seconds.label: Max Seconds
max_seconds.description: Bounded run duration. `null` = unbounded (runs until killed; health sensor auto-restarts).

max_messages.label: Max Messages
max_messages.description: Optional cap on total messages consumed before exit.

transform.label: Transform
transform.description: Polars ops (same shape as polars_pipeline): filter / with_columns / select / drop / rename / cast / drop_nulls / fill_null / sort / limit / unique.

sink.label: Sink
sink.description: `{kind: table | duckdb, resource_key, table, schema?, if_exists?: append|replace, dedup_on?: [col1, col2, ...]}`. `kind: duckdb` uses register-and-INSERT — 10-100x faster than SQLAlchemy `table`. `dedup_on:` when set, skips rows whose key tuple already exists in the target (NOT-EXISTS anti-join). For Kafka replays: `dedup_on: [_topic, _partition, _offset]` gives effective exactly-once semantics at zero user cost (the consumer already adds those columns to every row). Sink writes are wrapped in a transaction — a crash mid-batch rolls back cleanly.

name: Streaming Consumer
